title: Plan C does NOT recover internal tool history — Claude's one-final-blob output makes per-tool checkpointing impossible cross-agent
body:
The Claude CLI is invoked with `claude -p --output-format json` and only emits one final JSON blob when the subprocess terminates. Internal tool-call boundaries inside Claude (which tools ran, in what order, with what outputs) are NOT externally observable — they're only present in the final blob, which is exactly what gets truncated when the wrapper kills the subprocess.

Codex CLI emits NDJSON and is more stream-friendly, so per-tool boundaries ARE observable for codex invocations. But Plan C must work cross-agent — the supervisor doesn't know which executor it's running until the result comes back. Designing for codex's stream model would leave claude with an inferior code path, and designing for claude's blob model means we never recover claude's internal tool history.

Reason: the design choice is to use ONLY *external observables* — output byte counts (whatever was captured before kill), worktree delta (git porcelain v1 snapshot before/after), exit/signal status, env-var fallback markers — and surface those as evidence. The diagnostic claim Plan C makes is about whether work landed, not about what work landed.

How to apply: F001's runner captures stdout/stderr buffers and worktree delta from the *outside* — no peek into the subprocess. F002's envelope evidence is built from what the runner sees, not from internal tool boundaries. The framing in plan.md is explicit: 'Plan C does not recover internal tool history; it makes timeout envelopes truthful, schema-valid, and useful enough that the supervisor no longer mistakes work-landed-but-wrapper-timed-out for zero progress.'

title: No new `audit_status` enum value — schema is locked; timeouts stay `blocked`
body:
The audit envelope schema (`claude/shared/schemas/audit.schema.json`) locks `audit_status` to the enum `signed_off | needs_changes | blocked | inconclusive | redaction_required`. Adding a new value like `partial` or `timeout_with_work` would require: (a) bumping `agent-conventions/schemas/audit.schema.json`, (b) regenerating the Pydantic models in `agent-conventions/python/`, (c) updating the signoff aggregator's vote-counting logic, (d) coordinating a subtree pull into DontPanic. Too much blast radius for this fix.

Reason: timeouts STAY `blocked`. F002 makes blocked envelopes diagnostically useful via the existing `validation_performed` field (a list of strings — flexible, no schema change) and via structured findings (which use the existing `correctness` category enum). The supervisor classifier in F003 reads the `validation_performed` markers to distinguish blocked-with-work from blocked-without-work — no enum extension needed.

How to apply: F002 acceptance #1 explicitly asserts schema round-trip cleanliness; #2-#6 use only existing fields. F003 acceptance #15 reaffirms no enum extensions. If a future plan needs `partial` as a first-class status, it ships as a separate agent-conventions schema bump with its own coordinated rollout.

title: Timeout configurability via env vars in v1; per-plan via schema-backed `loop_caps.subprocess_timeout_seconds` deferred
body:
`loop_caps` in the plan schema has `additionalProperties: false`, so adding `subprocess_timeout_seconds` would require a schema bump. Plan C ships env-var configurability and defers per-plan to a future slice (which would either bump the schema OR add a parser-owned `executor_caps:` frontmatter block popped before schema validation).

Locked env-var contract:

- `DONTPANIC_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` — default 600, min 30, max 7200. Out-of-range values fall back to default + emit a marker.
- `DONTPANIC_SUBPROCESS_GRACE_SECONDS` — default 15, min 1, max 120. Same fallback semantics.
- Unparseable values (e.g., `foo`) → default + marker.
- Absent env var → default, no marker.
- Invalid values NEVER crash dispatch — defaults always apply, fallback marker is informational only.

Reason: minimum-blast-radius. Operators can configure long-running plans via env-set-once-then-dispatch; per-plan configurability is a stronger contract that needs schema work and shouldn't be conflated with this fix.

How to apply: F001 acceptance #4-#6 lock the parsing semantics. The validation marker format is `env_invalid: <VAR>=<value> (out of range [<lo>,<hi>]) | (unparseable), fell back to <default>` — surfaces in F002's `validation_performed` so operators can see when their env var was rejected.

title: Sidecar partials live under `audit/partials/`, NOT inline in audit JSON — schema has `additionalProperties: false`
body:
The audit envelope schema's `additionalProperties: false` means new top-level fields like `partial_stdout_path` would fail validation. Plan C uses sidecar files instead.

Layout:

- `docs/plans/<plan-id>/audit/partials/<audit_id>.stdout.txt`
- `docs/plans/<plan-id>/audit/partials/<audit_id>.stderr.txt`
- (or `.bin` suffix when bytes are not UTF-8 decodable)

The path is referenced from `validation_performed` (which IS schema-valid — it's a list of arbitrary strings) as a marker like `partial_stdout_path=audit/partials/<audit_id>.stdout.txt`.

Reason: respects the existing schema; gives operators a single place to look for partial output (`audit/partials/`) without inflating audit JSON file size; keeps audit JSON byte-stable for non-timeout cases.

How to apply: F002 step 4 introduces `_write_partial_sidecars()`. F002 acceptance #7-#9 lock the on-disk layout. The `audit/partials/` directory is per-plan (under each plan's own audit/ tree); committed alongside the rest of the audit/ artifacts when present.

title: F001 runner uses `Popen(start_new_session=True)` + `os.killpg(SIGTERM)` → grace → `os.killpg(SIGKILL)` — NOT `subprocess.run`
body:
`subprocess.run(... timeout=N)` only signals the immediate child. If that child has spawned grandchildren (e.g., the Claude CLI exec'ing tool subprocesses), they survive the wrapper kill and become orphaned — they keep consuming resources, may write to disk after the runner has 'returned', and can produce ghost effects on subsequent dispatches.

Locked pattern:

```python
proc = Popen(cmd, stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE, cwd=cwd, env=env, start_new_session=True)
pgid = proc.pid  # session leader's pid IS the pgid
try:
    stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(timeout=timeout_seconds)
    timed_out = False
except TimeoutExpired:
    try:
        os.killpg(pgid, SIGTERM)
    except OSError:
        pass  # group already dead
    try:
        stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(timeout=grace_seconds)
        grace_period_used = True
    except TimeoutExpired:
        try:
            os.killpg(pgid, SIGKILL)
        except OSError:
            pass
        stdout, stderr = proc.communicate()  # no timeout — group is dead
        grace_period_used = True  # used + escalated
    timed_out = True
```

Reason: process groups via `start_new_session=True` mean the child becomes a session leader, and its descendants inherit the same process group. `os.killpg(pgid, signal)` then signals the WHOLE group, killing grandchildren too. `subprocess.run` doesn't expose this; we must use `Popen` directly.

How to apply: F001 step 2 codifies the pattern. F001 acceptance #2 verifies via a parametric test that forks a child-spawning-grandchild and confirms the grandchild is killed when the parent times out (not just orphaned). The killpg calls are wrapped in try/except OSError so already-dead groups don't raise.

title: Worktree detection lives in the runner, optional, NEVER fails dispatch
body:
F001's runner snapshots `git status --porcelain=v1` before Popen and after the subprocess terminates; diff = `worktree_changed`. But git can fail in many ways: not installed, cwd not a repo, repo corrupt, git command timeouts, permission errors. None of these should fail the dispatch.

Locked contract:

- If both before-snapshot and after-snapshot succeed: `worktree_changed = (before != after)`. Boolean.
- If either snapshot fails (any reason): `worktree_changed = None`, surfaced to F002 as the marker `worktree_changed=unknown`.
- The git-status calls are wrapped in try/except: `FileNotFoundError` (git missing), `subprocess.CalledProcessError` (git error), `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` (git hung — bound the helper itself with a short timeout, e.g., 5s), generic `OSError`.
- Dispatch never raises because of git issues; it degrades to `worktree_changed=None`.

Reason: cross-platform robustness. CI environments without git installed, ephemeral cwd that isn't a repo, fresh-clone scenarios where the helper might race git's lock — all should still allow dispatch to proceed. The 'unknown' marker is honest evidence; the auditor and supervisor classifier (F003) treat 'unknown' as 'don't claim work landed' (so timeout + unknown does NOT trigger the F002 finding, and F003's classifier does NOT exclude unknown from no-progress counting — that was the 'no over-correction' guarantee).

How to apply: F001 step 4 + acceptance #8-#11 lock the helper. F002 step 3(c) ensures the finding only emits on `worktree_changed=true` (not unknown). F003 acceptance #2 + #6 verify the no-over-correction property — `worktree_changed=false` and `worktree_changed=unknown` BOTH still count toward no-progress.

title: F002 timeout-with-work finding uses existing `correctness` category — no new findings categories
body:
The findings `category` field is schema-locked to an enum. The existing values include `correctness`, `security`, `style`, `test_coverage`, `documentation`, `performance` (and possibly others; locked at `agent-conventions` schema). Adding a new category like `infrastructure` or `subprocess_management` would require a schema bump.

Locked finding shape for timeout + worktree_changed=true:

- `severity`: `medium`
- `category`: `correctness` (existing schema-locked enum value)
- `issue`: `"executor timed out after observable worktree changes; partial work landed on disk"`
- `evidence`: `"<runtime>s timeout exceeded; <N> stdout bytes captured; git status --porcelain=v1 differs before/after"`
- `recommendation`: `"audit the working-tree changes and either re-dispatch or accept on direct review"`

Reason: `correctness` is the closest existing fit — the run produced an inconsistent envelope-vs-disk state, which IS a correctness concern even if no specific code is wrong. The severity is `medium` because the supervisor's classification (F003) handles it cleanly; it's not a code bug, it's a workflow-state observation that operators or downstream tooling should know about.

How to apply: F002 step 3(c) + acceptance #5 lock the finding shape. F002 acceptance #6 explicitly asserts no false-positive emission for non-timeout / non-worktree-changed cases.

title: F003 may diff `circuit_breakers.py` — Plan B's zero-diff invariant explicitly does NOT carry to Plan C; replacement contract: no threshold/default/status changes
body:
Plan B's D001 + AC #13 enforced `git diff --stat scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/circuit_breakers.py == 0` because Plan B was scoped to human gates only. Plan C IS scoped to the no-progress / diminishing-returns classifier, which may live partially in `circuit_breakers.py` (depending on the codebase's current factoring). So Plan C may diff that file.

Replacement contract for Plan C F003:

- May add / modify the timeout-with-work classifier helper in `circuit_breakers.py` (or `supervisor.py`, wherever it naturally lives).
- May NOT change: terminal-status string literals, breaker enum values, threshold defaults, no_progress_threshold arithmetic, diminishing-returns window size, any breaker firing condition unrelated to timeout-with-work.
- F003 acceptance #7 verifies via grep of the diff: only logic changes tied to the timeout-with-work classifier are allowed; the listed forbidden change patterns must NOT appear.

Reason: scope clarity. Plan C is allowed to fix what it's fixing; it's NOT allowed to drift into broader breaker tuning. The grep-of-diff acceptance gives the auditor a clear yes/no for whether F003 stayed in its lane.

How to apply: F003 step 5(f) + acceptance #7 lock the contract. The audit-focus addendum in plan.md (item 4) calls this out for the volley auditor. If the implementer's diff in circuit_breakers.py contains forbidden change patterns, the auditor flags it as a feature_defect.

title: Per-feature execution path: F001 direct, F002 direct, F003 volley
body:
F001 (shared subprocess runner) is a pure refactor + new helper module + tests. Mechanical, deterministic acceptance. Direct path.

F002 (timeout evidence in audit envelopes) is additive within the existing schema. The behavior is determined by F001's `SubprocessResult` shape; F002's job is to render that shape into envelope fields. AC-driven, mechanical. Direct path.

F003 (supervisor classifier) is a real semantic change to how the no-progress / diminishing-returns detectors interpret envelopes. The risk surface includes: missed call sites, classification edge cases (worktree_changed=unknown, missing markers, malformed envelopes), false-positive over-correction (legitimate no-progress mistakenly excluded), false-negative under-correction (timeout-with-work mistakenly counted). These are exactly the failure modes adversarial review catches.

Reason: volley quota is finite. Direct for the mechanical features; volley for the semantic one. Same per-feature pattern as plan 003 D010.

How to apply: F001 + F002 ship via direct landings (separate commits or bundled); F003 ships via `dontpanic dispatch-from-plan ... --feature F003`. F003 inherits Plan B's lifecycle-staged gates: `pre_impl` clears before iter 0, `pre_merge` clears only if the auditor signs off + before signoff_writer writes passes:true. Plan C is the first dogfood of Plan B's staged-gate behavior.

title: Historical `docs/plans/` directories are durable records — only this plan's own new dir touches docs/plans/
body:
Inherited from Plan A's D003 + Plan B's D008 + the operator-tightened wording on Plan A's commit boundary: 'no docs/plans/ churn' means no historical plan dirs outside this plan's own new directory.

Not touched by this plan:
- Any committed slug under `docs/plans/2026-04-XX-*`, `docs/plans/2026-05-01-*`, `docs/plans/2026-05-03-*`, `docs/plans/2026-05-04-001-*`, or `docs/plans/2026-05-04-002-*`
- File contents under those dirs — evidence files, decisions.jsonl entries, audit envelope JSON, signoff JSON, transcripts, INBOX.md
- Memory entries under `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/*.md`
- The agent-conventions subtree at `claude/shared/`

Reason: durability of audit history. Same logic as Plan A/B — historical plans encode what shipped under what conditions; rewriting them erases evidence trails.

How to apply: F001/F002/F003 acceptance items each include a `git diff --name-only HEAD` assertion that shows zero entries under `docs/plans/` outside `2026-05-04-003-fix-subprocess-timeout-envelope-durability/`. Pre-merge sweep verifies.

title: Plan C is the first dogfood of Plan B's lifecycle-staged gates — F003's volley itself runs under staged evaluation
body:
Plan B (commit `dc9c6cd`) shipped lifecycle-staged human gates: `pre_impl` fires before implementer iteration 0, `pre_merge` fires only on candidate-success path before `signoff_writer.write_signoff(passes=True)`. Plan C is the first plan to run AFTER Plan B merged, so its own volley (F003) is the first dogfood of the staged-gate behavior.

What to expect:

- Dispatch will pause on `pre_impl` only. The operator clears it via `dontpanic approve <plan-id> pre_impl` (or `--gate pre_impl` resume), and the implementer fires for iter 0.
- `pre_merge` does NOT fire upfront. It only fires if the auditor signs off and the supervisor is about to write `passes:true`.
- If F003's volley itself terminates on a non-success path (`needs_changes`, `stopped_no_progress`, `stopped_cap`, `stopped_diminishing_returns`, timeout, breaker stop), `pre_merge` is NEVER evaluated — Plan B's D005 + AC #5 contract.
- Plan C is itself a meta-dogfood of the timeout-with-work fix. F001+F002 will already be merged when F003 dispatches, so F003's envelopes will carry the new evidence markers — but the OLD classifier (which F003 is fixing) will still misfire on them. Expected resolution: accept F003 on direct review per the established F002/F003-of-plan-003 + Plan B pattern, OR (less likely) the volley terminates cleanly because impl iterations happen to fit in the deadline.

Reason: this is the first plan to exercise Plan B's runtime behavior end-to-end, AND F003's classifier change applies retroactively to Plan B-shaped runs (including potentially Plan C's own). Documenting the expectation here so the operator and any future reviewer understands the meta-loop.

How to apply: this is informational; no acceptance items reference it. The audit-focus addendum in plan.md notes that F003's volley may itself produce timeout-with-work envelopes and that accept-on-direct-review is the established pattern when it does.

title: Plan C locked at 2026-05-04 with all seven operator tightenings absorbed
body:
Operator reviewed the v2 proposal and locked it. Seven specific tightenings were absorbed into the locked decisions:

1. **No `partial_stdout_path` / `partial_stderr_path` fields inside audit JSON** — `additionalProperties: false`. Sidecars under `audit/partials/`, referenced from `validation_performed` (D004).
2. **F001 runner uses `Popen(start_new_session=True)` + `killpg`-based termination, NOT `subprocess.run`** (D005).
3. **Env vars need strict parsing**: bounds + fallback + non-crashing on invalid values (D003).
4. **F002 finding uses existing `correctness` category** — no new findings categories (D007).
5. **Worktree detection in the runner, optional, never fails dispatch** (D006).
6. **F003 may touch `circuit_breakers.py`**; replacement contract: no threshold/default/status changes (D008).
7. **Per-feature execution paths confirmed**: F001 direct, F002 direct, F003 volley (D009).

Key framing the operator gave at lock time:

> Plan C does not recover internal tool history; it makes timeout envelopes truthful, schema-valid, and useful enough that the supervisor no longer mistakes 'work landed but wrapper timed out' for 'zero progress.'

This framing is preserved in plan.md's description and motivation sections (D001 + D002 codify the technical constraints behind it).

Lock authority: operator (this turn). Plan C flipped `status: draft` → `status: active` directly at draft time (the operator's lock signal was unambiguous: 'With those tightenings, I'd lock it.'). Implementation may begin.

Next steps:
1. F001 lands direct (commit boundary: shared runner + executor delegation + tests + post-implementation sweep)
2. F002 lands direct (commit boundary: audit envelope evidence + sidecar writer + tests + sweep)
3. F003 volleys (commit boundary: pre-volley audit-focus addendum is already inside plan.md; lock-commit IS the pre-volley addendum); dispatch via `dontpanic dispatch-from-plan ... --feature F003`; expect Plan B staged-gate behavior to govern; accept-on-direct-review if 600s timeout pattern recurs.

title: F001 close-out — shared subprocess runner shipped direct
body:
F001 landed via the locked direct path. The duplicated executor `subprocess.run(... timeout=600)` calls were replaced with `subprocess_runner.run_subprocess()`, which uses `Popen(start_new_session=True)`, bounded env-var parsing, process-group SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL timeout handling, stdout/stderr byte capture, and optional git worktree delta detection. Both Claude and Codex executors now attach the internal `SubprocessResult` to `DispatchResult` for F002 consumption, without adding audit-envelope fields.

Verification on the operator machine: baseline before edits was 886 passed, 6 skipped with `test_ec5_classifier.py` excluded; focused F001 suite (`test_subprocess_runner.py` + executor argv tests) was 36 passed, 6 skipped; full orchestrate suite after F001 was 899 passed, 6 skipped (exact +13 from the new runner tests); ruff check clean; ruff format --check clean; sanitization clean (677 files); grep for `subprocess.run(... timeout=` under `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/executors/` returned zero hits; no docs/plans diffs outside this plan's own directory.

F001 is flipped to passes:true. F002 remains next and owns audit-envelope evidence rendering / sidecar partials; F003 remains volley and owns supervisor classifier semantics.

title: F002 close-out — timeout evidence layered into existing audit envelope schema; sidecars under audit/partials/
body:
F002 shipped via direct path. The implementation lives entirely in `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/audit_writer.py` with five new module-level helpers: `_render_worktree_value`, `_timeout_summary_block`, `_timeout_markers`, `_timeout_finding`, and `_write_partial_sidecars`. `build_audit()` consumes `result.subprocess_result` (F001's threaded field) when present and timed-out, layering markers into `validation_performed`, structured context into `summary`, and a `correctness/medium` finding when worktree changes were observed. All non-timeout paths are byte-stable: helpers are no-ops when subprocess_result is None or when timed_out=False.

What landed:

- `audit_writer.py`: 5 helpers + `build_audit()` extension, ~140 added lines, ruff/format clean.
- `tests/test_audit_envelope_timeout_evidence.py`: 21 new tests across 6 classes — schema validity + byte stability (4 tests), structured timeout summary (2), validation_performed markers (5 with parametric ternary worktree), env fallback markers (1), timeout finding emission/non-emission (4), sidecar partials (4 covering UTF-8, .bin, empty bytes, both streams), boundary discipline (1 — circuit_breakers.py untouched).

Verification:

- Targeted F002: 21 passed in 0.23s.
- Pre-existing audit_writer regression set (test_audit_writer_normalize, test_audit_writer_f002_supervisor_integration, test_audit_filename_feature_id): 42 passed.
- Full orchestrate suite (excl. test_ec5_classifier.py per Plan D scope): 920 passed, 6 skipped. Baseline before F002 was 899+6 → +21 net = exactly the new F002 tests; ZERO regressions in any pre-existing test.
- Ruff check + format check clean across canonical tree.
- Sanitization: 0 findings, 679 files scanned.

Schema discipline confirmed:

- `audit_status` stays `blocked` for timeouts (D002 — no enum extension).
- No new top-level audit JSON fields (D004 — `additionalProperties: false` respected).
- Sidecars at `audit/partials/<audit_id>.{stdout,stderr}.{txt,bin}`, referenced ONLY via `validation_performed` markers.
- Finding uses existing `correctness/medium` (D007 — no new category enum).
- Worktree detection optional (D006 — never fails dispatch; renders as `unknown` for non-git cwd).
- `circuit_breakers.py` untouched in F002 (boundary preserved per AC #12; F003 may diff per D008).

F003 (volley) is unblocked — `depends_on: [F002]` is satisfied. F003 will read F002's `validation_performed` markers (specifically `worktree_changed=true` paired with `audit_status: blocked`) to classify timeout-with-work envelopes correctly in the no-progress / diminishing-returns detectors.

Plan status: F001 + F002 passes:true. F003 remains passes:false until volley closes out.
